slides.title: Learning Check: Find the First Audit Move

options.text: Start from one witnessed audit file where the candidate handled a generative AI office tool well but struggled with impact-assessment. and observe how the AI changes work, responsibility or decision flow.
options.feedback: Good route. It turns the discussion from general assurance into sampled evidence.

options.label: Collect policies first
options.text: Ask for all AI policies and procedures before selecting a real use sample.
options.feedback: Policies matter, but starting only from documents can miss how AI is actually used.

options.text: Accept the comfortable answer without testing how AI affects the actual workflow.
options.feedback: That answer may be true in form, but the auditor still needs evidence of real use and impact.

slides.title: Professional Boundary Wording
slides.subtitle: Finding language should stay inside the sampled evidence boundary.
bullets: For the sampled authorization decision, the certification body should limit or stage authorization until witnessed evidence demonstrates competence in impact assessment, lifecycle evidence and finding language for higher-impact AI systems.
Avoid replacing technical, clinical, legal or business judgement with an audit opinion.
State the sampled object, the criterion, the evidence gap and the management-system consequence.

hero.label: Professional boundary
hero.value: The finding should sound fair, specific and useful for improvement.
hero.note: The learner is not replacing technical or business judgement. The learner is judging whether the AIMS evidence supports the sampled route.

coach.think: Good wording protects both the auditor and the auditee.
coach.why: A narrow finding is easier to defend and easier for the client to correct.

slides.title: Learning Check: Keep the Audit Boundary
slides.subtitle: Pause after Slide 09 and choose wording that stays evidence-based.
slides.question: Which conclusion style is strongest for a training audit discussion?

options.label: Bounded wording
options.text: For the sampled authorization decision, the certification body should limit or stage authorization until witnessed evidence demonstrates competence in impact assessment, lifecycle evidence and finding language for higher-impact AI systems.
options.feedback: Strong. It names the sample, the evidence gap and the audit boundary.

options.label: Broad judgement
options.text: The AI system is unsafe and the organization is not ready for certification.
options.feedback: That overreaches. The auditor should not jump beyond the sampled evidence.

options.label: No issue
options.text: No issue exists because the organization gives a comfortable explanation.
options.feedback: A comfortable answer does not remove the need to test implementation and impact.

slides.coaching: Good finding language is narrow enough to be fair and specific enough to be useful. The hidden audit issue here is: Course success is important, but it does not prove competence for every AI context, sector risk, technical boundary or finding judgement.
